key_findings: Ant venom peptides (Ta3a, poneratoxin, Rm4a, Mri1a) cause nocifensive behaviour in mice by delaying inactivation and shifting activation of Nav channels, mainly Nav1.6/Nav1.7.
The peptides are vertebrate-selective, far more potent in mice than in blowflies, consistent with a defensive role.
